text:
Sidney Crosby passed Marcel Dionne on Saturday in Los Angeles and now sits alone in sixth on the NHL's all-time scoring list with 1,772 points, 26 behind Ron Francis. It came in a 5-2 win that ended a four-game winless run. That should be the whole story. Instead the Crosby headlines are about retirement, with a Sportskeeda headline quoting a Penguins insider: "The end might not be too far off."

Evgeni Malkin's future is in the same conversation, with reports that he must submit a three-team trade list and Darren Dreger linking him to Minnesota. The Penguins are 6-9-2 after a ten-game stretch that Ryan Wilson of Hockey Hot Stove called make or break before it started.

Our numbers say they're unlucky more than bad. Pittsburgh takes 52 percent of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances), and our race model thinks it has dropped 3.8 points it deserved. The power play is the drag: 0.44 expected goals a game, against 0.9 for Carolina. Ben Kindel had two points in his return, and Erik Karlsson has moved into the top ten all time in points by a defenseman. Our simulations put the playoffs at 20 percent. Watch Malkin's list. That's the first domino.
headline: Crosby climbs as the Penguins wonder how long
